zara_csm: Drafting a one-page customer-facing runbook: 'Latency smoothing & prefetch coalescing' 7 goal is a concise checklist CSMs can use during onboarding + two tiny paste-in client snippets (Go + curl). Want quick eyes.

mike_eng: Love the title. Can we include a short plain-language explanation for customers: 'coalescing = grouping nearby requests to reduce repeated work / backend load'? Keep it friendly.

zara_csm: Yes. Proposed customer blurb: 'If your app sends many short requests (typing, autosave), enable coalescing: buffer events for 80-250ms and send as a single request. This smooths bursts without changing model semantics.'

yuki_sre: Add jitter guidance: 5-18% randomization on the buffer window to avoid synchronized flushes across clients. Also recommend a max in-flight cap per session (e.g., 3) to prevent buildup.

mike_eng: Add prefetch window guidance too: small prefetch (0.5-1s) for conversational continuations; larger prefill windows for predicted heavy flows. Call out cost/latency tradeoffs: prefetch reduces cold latency but increases tokens billed.

zara_csm: Good. For cache hygiene, propose canonical key: tenant|route|conversation_prefix_hash|model_tag. Recommend conversation prefix TTL 15-45s depending on UX, rerank/windowed cache 2-15m, persistent embeddings 12-48h. Note: avoid embedding user session IDs in prompt hash.

marty_platform: Monitoring additions: watch coalesced batch size distribution, 95p token latency, and delta in per-tenant token rate after enabling prefetch. Escalation trigger idea: if median batch size drops >50% from baseline and 95p latency grows >20% => investigatory flag.

yuki_sre: Renewal-watch heuristic (compact): any of the following in 30 days -> add to renewal-watchlist and schedule an enablement review: (a) >3 onboarding stalls >24h, (b) average eval pass-rate <75% over 14 days, (c) 2+ customer-facing sev incidents. Tag root cause options: quality, latency, or cost surprise.

zara_csm: Nice. Can we add two ready-to-send outreach snips? Short + technical.

mike_eng: Short: "We observed bursty traffic from your integration during onboarding. We can enable client coalescing and a temporary prefetch cap for a 10-minute test. When's a good time?"

marty_platform: Technical: "Quick patch: buffer user events for 120ms + 10% jitter, send max batch size 8. Updated prompt hashing: exclude ephemeral session tokens. We'll validate on your eval slice after the change."

zara_csm: Adding troubleshooting checklist for CSMs: (1) confirm coalescing buffer + jitter enabled client-side, (2) confirm cache-key shape and TTLs, (3) check model_tag (pinned if quality-sensitive), (4) run eval subset and compare pass-rate, (5) check Console traces and recent deploys.

yuki_sre: Also include fallback guidance: if customers see quality regressions after batching, try: (a) lower batch size, (b) preserve original prompt ordering, (c) pin model variant. And include a note: "Always re-run eval slice after changes."

mike_eng: Pasteable Go micro-coalescer (very small):
```go
// micro-coalescer: buffer events for 100-250ms, max batch 8
func Coalesce(ctx context.Context, in <-chan Request, out chan<- []Request){
  buf := make([]Request, 0, 8)
  timer := time.NewTimer(time.Hour)
  defer timer.Stop()
  for{
    select{
    case req := <-in:
      buf = append(buf, req)
      if len(buf) == 1 { timer.Reset(120 * time.Millisecond) }
      if len(buf) >= 8 { out <- buf; buf = buf[:0]; timer.Stop() }
    case <-timer.C:
      if len(buf) > 0 { out <- buf; buf = buf[:0] }
    }
  }
}
```

zara_csm: And a tiny curl example showing the backpressure header we suggest we support: X-RW-Coalesce: level (0..1).

marty_platform: curl snippet:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-RW-Coalesce: 0.8" \
  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```
Clients should interpret >=0.7 as signal to apply aggressive coalescing/backoff.

yuki_sre: Add small FAQ item: "Does coalescing change outputs?" Answer: No, if prompt order, separators, and tokenization are preserved. Coalescing only groups requests; it can affect latency and billing. Re-run eval slice after changes.
